chunks: From him, from Ja'far and al-Mithammi, and al-Hasan ibn Hammad, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqqaq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a group of people disputed over a road, some saying it was seven cubits wide and others saying it was four cubits wide, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is five cubits.'
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed width of a public road according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in case of dispute?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the dispute over road width by selecting the arithmetic mean of the conflicting claims (four and seven cubits), a method reflecting the principle of *al-wasat* (moderation) in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, illustrates the practical application of equitable arbitration in resolving communal property disputes, emphasizing fairness over rigid adherence to either extreme.
